findings.summary: External-data webhook (POST integrations/external-data/webhooks/:providerId) resolves the target tenant from a fully client-supplied X-Tenant-ID header, while the HMAC signature check in ExternalDataExchangeService.ingestWebhook/assertSignature is validated against a single global per-provider secret (EXTERNAL_DATA_WEBHOOK_SECRET[_PROVIDER]) read from env config, not a per-tenant credential. Unlike AutentiqueService/DocuSignService (which resolve tenant server-side from a doc/envelope id already stored on the contract, never from client input), this endpoint lets any caller who knows the shared provider secret pick an arbitrary target tenant via the header, so the signature proves payload authenticity but not tenant scoping -- a cross-tenant write is possible against any entityId the attacker can guess/obtain for the target tenant. The P0-A billing-gate-skip reasoning (external event already happened) is sound in isolation, but it assumes tenant resolution here is as trustworthy as the Autentique/DocuSign peers, which it is not.

findings.summary: ExternalDataExchangeService.ingestWebhook reimplements webhook idempotency inline (raw webhookEvents.findOne/save on the same DataSource) instead of using the canonical WebhookService.ingest() used by Autentique/DocuSign, and its dedup check is weaker: it treats ANY prior row with the same external_id as a permanent duplicate regardless of status (line ~332: 'const duplicate = await this.webhookEvents!.findOne({ where: { external_id: externalId } }); if (duplicate) return { duplicate: true ... }'), whereas WebhookService.ingest() correctly distinguishes PROCESSED (true duplicate) from PENDING/FAILED (legitimate retry, reprocessed). A provider retrying a genuinely failed external-data reconciliation event will be silently swallowed as a duplicate forever after the first attempt, with no way to reconcile -- the opposite failure mode of a double-apply, but still a broken retry/idempotency contract, and a second competing implementation of the same 'webhook ingestion' concept per naming-canonical.md.
findings.justification: external-data-exchange.service.ts ingestWebhook dedupe now only short-circuits as a true duplicate when the prior webhook_events row for external_id is WebhookEventStatus.PROCESSED; PENDING/FAILED rows are reused and reprocessed (status reset to PENDING, retry_count incremented), matching WebhookService.ingest's identical established pattern. Added two regression tests (reprocess-on-non-terminal-status and true-duplicate-on-PROCESSED). Ran external-data-exchange.service.spec.ts (9 passed) once an unrelated pre-existing ShareEntity field-rename compile error in the same file (buildSocietyPayload, titular_nome/papel/percentual -> holder_name/role/percentage) was resolved by concurrent in-flight work outside this task's scope.

findings.summary: AutentiqueService.handleWebhook always returns { received: true } with HTTP 200 even when processSignedContract throws (catch block only logs + webhookSvc.markProcessed(id,'failed') + best-effort activity log, never rethrows). findings.summary: runDunningCycle (line 123) processes tenants from listTenantIdsRequiringDunningAttention() in a fully sequential for-loop with a plain await per tenant (no Promise.all/concurrency limit). Each iteration opens its own runInTenantContext transaction (BEGIN + 3x set_config + readStateRaw SELECT + getSettings SELECT, plus for escalating tenants an UPDATE + audit.log INSERT + COMMIT = up to ~8-10 DB round trips) and one BullMQ/Redis enqueueNotification round trip. At an assumed 15-25ms per round trip (typical pooled/cloud Postgres + Redis), that is roughly 150-250ms of pure network latency per tenant, fully serialized. Given the job runs once per 24h (DAY_MS in onApplicationBootstrap), this only becomes a wall-clock/cadence risk at an unrealistic scale (on the order of 100k-500k+ tenants simultaneously in payment_grace/read_only/suspended before the run approaches multi-hour duration); the more concrete near-term risk is tenant-visible: at a plausible 5k-10k tenants in a restricted billing state, the cycle takes minutes and delays notification delivery to tenants queued near the end by that same margin, since nothing runs concurrently. Verified NOT an issue: idx_tenant_billing_state_status (20260701000001_BillingEnforcement.ts line 54) already indexes tenant_billing_state.status, so the enumeration query in billing-enforcement.service.ts:104-111 is index-supported, not a full scan.
findings.justification: Verified: dunning.service.ts now implements bounded-concurrency worker pool for per-tenant processing (comment + dedicated spec test cite this finding id) instead of a fully sequential loop.

findings.summary: Duplicate billing notifications under concurrent/multi-replica runDunningCycle: BillingEnforcementService.suspendTenant/read_only-transition (billing-enforcement.service.ts applyOverrideAndEscalation L462-477, suspendTenant L343-366, auditStateChange L501-515) each issue their own bare 'UPDATE tenant_billing_state SET status_changed_at = now()' with no advisory lock / SELECT FOR UPDATE / overlap guard. Two concurrent invocations of processTenant() for the same tenant at the exact moment it crosses a payment_grace->read_only or ->suspended boundary (real trigger: onApplicationBootstrap's setInterval has zero cross-instance leader election/lock, so N horizontally-scaled API replicas each run their own daily cycle -- a rolling restart/redeploy makes all replicas fire onApplicationBootstrap near-simultaneously) each read the same before-state, each perform the status-mutating UPDATE, and each independently bump status_changed_at with a DIFFERENT now() timestamp. dunning.service.ts L189-190 derives the BullMQ dedup jobId from that per-call status_changed_at, so the two calls compute two DIFFERENT jobIds and BOTH notifQueue.add() calls succeed (confirmed against node_modules/bullmq's addStandardJob-9.lua / handleDuplicatedJob.lua: dedup is jobId-existence based, so two distinct jobIds are never deduped) -- the tenant receives duplicate billing.hard_suspend/soft_suspend_warning/payment_reminder notifications (both the queued NotificationsProcessor-persisted one and the unconditional this.ws.sendToTenant() call at L153, which has zero dedup of its own regardless of transition) for a single logical status transition. No test in dunning.service.spec.ts or billing-enforcement.service.spec.ts exercises concurrent/overlapping invocations.
findings.justification: Verified: dunning.service.ts's processTenant now takes a Postgres transaction-scoped advisory lock (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock) keyed on tenant id, serializing concurrent getState()/escalation attempts across replicas; comment explicitly cites this finding id.

findings.summary: Poison-message: a permanently-failed dunning notification job is never resent for that transition. jobId is dunning-notify:tenantId:status:status_changed_at (stable across cycles absent a real transition per design). notifQueue.add's per-job override only sets removeOnComplete:{age:30d}; removeOnFail is NOT overridden and inherits the shared 'notifications' queue's default removeOnFail:1000 (apps/api/src/queues/queue.module.ts L239-242, count-based retention, not time-based) -- confirmed against node_modules/bullmq/dist/cjs/commands/addStandardJob-9.lua + includes/handleDuplicatedJob.lua: Queue.add() with a jobId whose Redis job-hash key still exists (in ANY state incl. 'failed') returns the existing job unchanged (emits a 'duplicated' event) instead of re-queuing/retrying. So if NotificationsProcessor.process() fails all 3 attempts for a given transition (e.g. a transient DB/websocket error), the tenant's suspension/read-only/payment_grace notification for that transition is silently dropped forever: every subsequent daily cycle recomputes the identical jobId (status unchanged) and BullMQ treats it as an already-seen duplicate, never retrying. Nothing surfaces this as needing manual redelivery -- no dead-letter table/alert specific to billing notifications, only the generic shared failed-jobs set.
findings.justification: Verified: dunning.service.ts now escalates/retries a permanently-failed notification job instead of silently treating it as a duplicate forever (comment + spec test cite this finding id).

findings.summary: Global TenantGuard (APP_GUARD, runs on every authenticated+tenant-header request) still checks TenantEntity.active as the guard's sole rejection condition, but no production writer sets active=false for billing suspension anymore after this session's dunning.service.ts/billing.service.ts rework -- the field defaults true and is now lifecycle-only (per billing.service.ts's own comment). autentique.service.ts, docusign.service.ts and external-data-exchange.service.ts each explicitly cite TenantGuard by name as 'the only other place tenants.active gets checked', yet tenant.guard.ts itself carries no equivalent annotation that this check is now vacuous for billing purposes, and neither tenant.guard.spec.ts nor guard-chain.integration.spec.ts exercises the active=false branch. Not a functional bypass today -- BillingEnforcementGuard runs immediately after TenantGuard in the same global APP_GUARD chain and independently blocks suspended/read_only tenants via tenant_billing_state with blanket-deny-except-allowlist coverage -- but it is an unaccounted-for reader with a latent-risk documentation/test gap: a future change that reorders/removes BillingEnforcementGuard could wrongly assume TenantGuard's active check still backs up billing enforcement.
findings.rootCause: The billing-enforcement rework (removal of hardSuspend/updateAdminTenant's active=false write) redefined tenants.active as lifecycle-only and added clarifying comments to the three Public() webhook readers that reference TenantGuard, but did not add the same clarifying comment or a pinning test to TenantGuard itself, the exact site those comments point to.

findings.summary: No failure-count/streak tracking exists for a tenant's dunning-cycle failures. findings.summary: ALWAYS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES/normalizePath comparison is case-sensitive and requires a literal lowercase /api/v<digits> prefix, but Express (platform-express, default routing) matches routes case-insensitively. A request like GET /Health or GET /API/V1/health is actually routed by Express to the real health/metrics controller, but the guard's case-sensitive startsWithAny check fails to recognize it as allowlisted, so a suspended tenant gets an incorrect 403 TENANT_SUSPENDED on a route that is supposed to be always-allowed (health checks, metrics scraping, /billing portal callbacks with non-canonical casing). Verified empirically: a minimal Express app with routes /health and /artists resolves GET /Health -> 200 (the health handler), confirming the case-insensitive match, while the guard code only checks path === prefix || path.startsWith(prefix + "/") against literal lowercase prefixes. This is a fail-closed defect (denies an always-allowed diagnostic route), not an authorization bypass -- it does not let a suspended tenant reach forbidden business functionality.
findings.rootCause: normalizePath()/startsWithAny() do string comparison against ALWAYS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES without lowercasing the incoming path or matching Express's case-insensitive route-matching semantics, and the /api/v-prefix strip regex has no 'i' flag.
findings.justification: billing-enforcement.guard.ts normalizePath now lowercases the path and the /api/v\d+ strip regex is case-insensitive (added 'i' flag), matching Express's own case-insensitive routing so a differently-cased path can't bypass the ALWAYS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES allowlist. Added regression test; ran billing-enforcement.guard.spec.ts (9 passed).

findings.summary: onApplicationBootstrap's setInterval fires runDunningCycle() every 24h with no in-flight guard/lock and no per-query timeout on the underlying DB calls (listTenantIdsRequiringDunningAttention/getState use ds.query() directly; database.module.ts only configures connectionTimeoutMillis for acquiring a pooled connection, not a statement_timeout for an already-running query). If a single cycle's DB call hangs, its promise never settles, the interval still fires a second overlapping runDunningCycle() 24h later, and this compounds (pool exhaustion) rather than failing fast or being visibly detectable as 'cycle N is still running'.
findings.justification: Verified: dunning.service.ts now has an in-flight guard (cycleInFlight) preventing overlapping runDunningCycle executions (comment + spec test cite this finding id).

findings.summary: Shadow-table copy+swap (CREATE inventory_items_new, INSERT..SELECT copy, then RENAME/DROP old) is not safe under concurrent app writes: rows INSERTed/UPDATEd into inventory_items by live traffic after the copy SELECT but before the final RENAME+DROP are silently lost -- the only integrity check (row-count compare) runs immediately after the copy, too early to catch this window. down() has the identical gap. No documented maintenance-window/write-freeze convention found in DATABASE.md or datasource.ts to rule this out for a live deploy; same pattern is shared by the ~24 sibling RebuildXInCanonicalFormOrder migrations.
findings.justification: Same systemic shadow-table copy+swap concurrency gap as find-239eff3b, shared by ~24 sibling migrations; needs a maintenance-window policy decision, not a code fix to an already-run migration.

findings.summary: applyOverrideAndEscalation's read_only-transition branch (lines 465-477) issues UPDATE tenant_billing_state SET status='read_only' with no WHERE status='payment_grace' guard and no row-version check, and applyManualOverride's own inline status_changed_at bump (lines 397-404, a second unsynchronized copy of the same 'bump status_changed_at on real transition' rule that auditStateChange centralizes for every other writer) is likewise a separate non-transactional statement after the initial upsert. Two concurrent getState() calls for the same tenant (e.g. two parallel HTTP requests hitting BillingEnforcementGuard, or a live request racing the DunningService sweep) that both read the pre-transition row before either write lands will both take the read_only branch, both call auditStateChange, and both persist a duplicate 'billing.read_only' audit_logs row with two different status_changed_at timestamps from two consecutive now() calls. Because DunningService.enqueueNotification's BullMQ dedup jobId is keyed on status_changed_at (dunning.service.ts line 189), this can defeat the 'exactly one notification per transition' guarantee (two jobIds enqueued for one logical transition) and leaves a duplicated, timestamp-inconsistent audit entry for a single real event — a race silently corrupting the audit timeline rather than the enforcement decision itself. Also flagged as a canonical-naming concern: two independent implementations of the status_changed_at-bump rule (auditStateChange vs. applyManualOverride's inline copy) is exactly the 'one business rule, one authoritative implementation' pattern naming-canonical.md calls a finding.
findings.justification: Verified: billing-enforcement.service.ts's read_only transition now uses an optimistic WHERE-status guard (comment + dedicated spec describe block cite this finding id), closing the concurrent-transition race.

findings.summary: Public unauthenticated lead-capture (submitPublicArtistApplication, line 326 gate in getPublicWorkspaceBySlug) checks only tenants.active/deleted_at/allow_public_registration, never tenant_billing_state.status. findings.summary: Pre-existing (not introduced this session, but directly load-bearing for the new blanket-deny guard): BillingEnforcementGuard treats 'no billing state row' as fail-open ('if (!state) return true' at billing-enforcement.guard.ts:61). findings.summary: Copy-and-swap physical rebuild of inventory_items (CREATE inventory_items_new -> INSERT...SELECT copy -> RENAME old/new -> DROP old) takes no lock on the source table before/during the copy. Between the INSERT...SELECT snapshot and the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock acquired only at the later 'RENAME TO inventory_items_old' statement, any concurrently committed INSERT/UPDATE against the live inventory_items table lands in the row that gets renamed to inventory_items_old and is then DROPped in the same transaction -- silent, permanent data loss on a live/populated DB with no maintenance window. The row-count guard (total vs newCount) only checks the initial copy step and cannot detect this later window; down() has the identical gap in reverse. findings.summary: artist_platform_profiles tem UNIQUE(tenant_id, artist_id, platform), mas essa constraint garante unicidade do estado ATUAL (uma linha por artista+plataforma), nao impede concorrencia: como o fluxo e UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, confirmado em ArtistPlatformProfilesService), duas syncs concorrentes para o mesmo (tenant,artist,platform) nao geram duas linhas 'pending' -- elas serializam no mesmo row via lock de UPSERT. A protecao real contra corrida logica (dois jobs simultaneos pisando um no outro) esta inteiramente na aplicacao (checagem sync_status==='pending' antes de reprocessar, linha 54 do service), sem lock otimista (sem coluna version/updated_at usada em WHERE) nem SELECT ... FOR UPDATE explicito no banco. Se o distributed-systems-reviewer confirmar corrida real no nivel da aplicacao, a mitigacao de banco recomendada e um UPDATE condicional (WHERE sync_status='pending' AND id=) para lock otimista barato, nao apenas o UNIQUE existente que so cobre criacao de linha duplicada.
findings.justification: Optimistic-lock/race-condition hardening for artist_platform_profiles UPSERT needs a distributed-systems-reviewer confirmation of real application-level races before deciding on a WHERE sync_status='pending' conditional-update pattern, per the finding's own conditional recommendation.

findings.summary: Race window: enqueueManualSync calls profiles.upsertPending() AFTER queue.add() succeeds (line ~171), but the worker (ArtistPlatformSyncProcessor.processInTenantContext) independently calls its own upsertPending at job start. If the worker picks up and completes the job (upsertSuccess/markFailed) before the producer's post-add upsertPending executes, the producer's late write overwrites the already-final 'success'/'failed' row back to 'pending' with no job left to resolve it — reintroducing a variant of the orphan-pending bug the reordering was meant to fix. Narrow but real under fast/local Redis or same-process workers.
findings.justification: Verified: artist-external-profile-sync.service.ts's enqueueManualSync no longer calls upsertPending after queue.add(); the worker is now the sole writer of 'pending' for the queued path, per the in-code comment addressing this exact finding.

findings.summary: webhook_events/payment_events/tenant_billing_state RLS policies use (app_current_tenant_id() IS NULL OR tenant_id = ...) as a system-path escape hatch: ANY authenticated-role connection with no tenant session context set gets full cross-tenant SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on these tables, not just the intended unauthenticated webhook path. Absence of context is the default state (DATABASE_SESSION_CONTEXT_ENABLED=false by default, only forced true when NODE_ENV=production per env.schema.ts) and is also the real state for BullMQ processors that never call runInTenantContext (email.processor.ts, ai-jobs.processor.ts, external-data.processor.ts).
findings.justification: Root-cause fix requires coupling: (1) new SQL helper app_is_system_context() checking current_setting('app.current_role',true)='system' replacing the ambiguous app_current_tenant_id() IS NULL branch on webhook_events/payment_events/tenant_billing_state RLS policies, AND (2) wiring billing-enforcement.service.ts (recordWebhookProcessed/markWebhookProcessed/markWebhookFailed) + billing.service.ts (recordLegacyWebhook) through DatabaseContextService.runInTenantContext({tenantId, role: tenantId ? undefined : 'system'}) so the Stripe webhook path explicitly declares system-path intent instead of relying on absent context. Shipping the SQL policy change alone without the code wiring would deny the real webhook path outright (production regression) since it currently sets no session context at all. This exact coupled change belongs to Wave 5 (BILLING/STRIPE full trace), which already owns webhook->persistence tracing end-to-end and will have the full call-graph context to wire it correctly and test it. Deferred with concrete design, not dropped.

findings.summary: Any tenant 'owner' can self-promote (or promote another member) to the global 'super_admin' role via PATCH /users/:id/role, bypassing the is_assignable=false restriction enforced only on the invite path, then use that role to access every other tenant's billing/audit/admin data via @RequireRole('super_admin') endpoints that are not tenant-scoped.

Default/normal runtime DB connection (DATABASE_URL) is the Supabase postgres superuser-equivalent role (confirmed by migration 20260803000002 comment: 'Toda migration deste projeto roda via DATABASE_URL conectado como postgres'), which bypasses RLS unconditionally regardless of FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The RLS-enforcing NOBYPASSRLS musicos_app role + session-context (SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id) only activates when DATABASE_SESSION_CONTEXT_ENABLED=true AND APP_DATABASE_URL is set. This combination is enforced only for NODE_ENV=production (env.schema.ts collectProductionAuthorityErrors); any other environment handling real tenant data (staging/preview under a different NODE_ENV) runs 100 percent of RLS as decorative, with tenant isolation resting entirely on application-level WHERE tenant_id filters.
findings.justification: Verified: env.schema.ts's collectProductionAuthorityErrors now gates on nodeEnv === 'production' OR 'staging' (comment cites this finding id), closing the RLS-decorative gap for staging environments.

findings.summary: BullMQ processors email.processor.ts, ai-jobs.processor.ts and external-data.processor.ts run DB queries via the shared DATA_SOURCE without ever calling DatabaseContextService.runInTenantContext, unlike notifications.processor.ts, marketing-publishing.processor.ts, market-benchmark-refresh.processor.ts, artist-platform-sync.processor.ts and schedulers (contract-expiry, invoice-overdue) which do wrap their work. When DATABASE_SESSION_CONTEXT_ENABLED=true these processors run through the NOBYPASSRLS musicos_app/authenticated connection with NO tenant session variable set: ordinary tenant_isolation policies (tenant_id = private_get_tenant_id()) fail-closed-deny their writes, while the system-path NULL-bypass policies (webhook_events/payment_events/tenant_billing_state) fail-open and grant unrestricted cross-tenant access -- tenant isolation for these paths depends entirely on the tenantId parameter application code passes through, not on RLS.

POST /users (create(), gated only @RequireRole('owner')) lets a tenant owner grant super_admin (or any non-assignable/higher-hierarchy role) to a brand-new member, bypassing the just-added is_assignable check and the hierarchy ceiling entirely

An owner can POST /users with role:'super_admin' and the DB row is created with role='super_admin' + a real role_id, granting every @RequireRole('super_admin') route platform-wide -- the exact privilege-escalation class the fix claims to close, via a sibling endpoint.

findings.summary: No event-ordering/staleness guard on Stripe subscription webhook writes: onSubUpdated (billing.service.ts:732-742) dispatches enforcement (activateTenant/startPaymentGrace/cancelTenant) purely from the payload of whichever event.type customer.subscription.updated/created delivery is processed, and upsertStripeSubscription (billing.service.ts:799-837, INSERT..ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) unconditionally overwrites billing_subscriptions.status/current_period_start/current_period_end/trial_ends_at/cancel_at_period_end with EXCLUDED values on every write -- no comparison against the incoming Stripe event's created timestamp or the subscription's current_period_start/updated-at vs the already-stored row. Stripe explicitly documents that webhook delivery order is not guaranteed (retries/network can reorder). Concrete scenario: Stripe emits E1 (subscription active, e.g. after a successful retry) then E2 (subscription past_due, an earlier failed-charge transition) but E2 is delivered/processed after E1 due to reordering or a stale queued retry; onSubUpdated processes E2 last and calls startPaymentGrace, silently reverting an already-corrected active tenant back into payment_grace -- or the reverse (a stale 'active' E1 delivered after a genuine 'past_due'/'cancelled' E2 calls activateTenant, silently restoring full access for a tenant who has actually stopped paying/cancelled). No payment_events dedup catches this because each Stripe retry/transition carries a distinct event.id (dedup is per-event.id, not per-subscription-state ordering). Distinct from find-d87bba6d (cross-table atomicity) and find-c64da2b1 (concurrent-read race) -- this is a single-writer correctness bug from processing events in receipt order instead of Stripe's authoritative event order.

Partial-failure webhook retry re-runs full side-effect set including one-shot domain events: if onCheckoutCompleted (billing.service.ts:660-730) throws partway through (e.g. subRepo/tenantRepo update succeeds but a later statement/network call fails), handleWebhook's catch (line 619-622) calls markWebhookFailed, and payment_events.status='failed' becomes reclaimable by recordWebhookProcessed (billing-enforcement.service.ts:245-275) on Stripe's next retry of the same event.id. The retry re-runs onCheckoutCompleted from the top: the repo upserts are idempotent (plain UPDATEs / ON CONFLICT), but this.ws.sendToTenant('billing:plan_upgraded', ...) (line 708) and this.events.emitTyped(DOMAIN_EVENTS.TENANT_CREATED, ...) (line 717-729) are NOT idempotent -- they unconditionally fire again. NotificationHandler (core/events/notification.handler.ts) persists a second 'Conta criada' NotificationEntity and broadcasts a second realtime toast for a single logical checkout. Low blast radius today (no email/provisioning side effect currently wired to TENANT_CREATED), but any future handler added to TENANT_CREATED (welcome email, workspace provisioning, billing analytics) would double-fire on every partial-failure retry with no dedup key available (no idempotency key derived from event.id passed through emitTyped).
onCheckoutCompleted's alreadyActive idempotency guard suppresses billing:plan_upgraded notification and TENANT_CREATED event for genuine plan upgrades, not just retries
findings.rootCause: The guard added for find-0b089515 compares org.billing_status (fetched before the write) to 'active' to detect a reclaimed/retried checkout. But a real second checkout (e.g. professional to enterprise upgrade while the org is already active) also has billing_status==='active' before the new checkout completes, since 'active' reflects any-active-plan state, not which plan or which checkout session. Because Stripe event-id deduplication (recordWebhookProcessed) already handles true retries earlier in the pipeline (returns 'duplicate' and short-circuits before onCheckoutCompleted runs), this new event-id checkout.session.completed for a genuine upgrade is not a duplicate, reaches onCheckoutCompleted, correctly updates billing_subscriptions/tenants/organizations rows to the new plan, calls enforcement.activateTenant, but then alreadyActive===true causes an early return that skips ws.sendToTenant('billing:plan_upgraded', ...) and the DOMAIN_EVENTS.TENANT_CREATED emission -- so the user/UI never learns about the upgrade via realtime or the domain event, even though the DB state is correct. The added spec test only covers the retry-after-partial-failure case (org already active before a RECLAIMED same-event retry), never a second genuine checkout while active, so this gap is untested.

findings.summary: onCheckoutCompleted's new subBefore lookup (SELECT ... WHERE s.org_id = :orgId .getOne()) assumes exactly one billing_subscriptions row per org_id, but only tenant_id and stripe_subscription_id have unique indexes (20260701000001_BillingEnforcement.ts) -- org_id itself only has a plain non-unique index (idx_billing_org_id). If more than one row ever shares an org_id (e.g. tenant re-provisioning, stale row left after a tenant swap), getOne() picks an arbitrary row with no ORDER BY, which can silently flip isRetryOfSameCheckout in either direction (false suppress of a genuine upgrade notification, or a duplicate re-notification).
findings.rootCause: DB schema never enforced org_id uniqueness on billing_subscriptions; the new retry-identity guard added in this fix relies on that unproven invariant without an ORDER BY/tiebreaker or a DB constraint to back it. Pre-existing sibling code (getSubscription) makes the same org_id .getOne() assumption, so this is a systemic gap the fix inherited rather than introduced, but it directly undermines the 'is subBefore guaranteed the right row' question this round was meant to close.
findings.justification: Fixing requires either a DB uniqueness constraint on billing_subscriptions.org_id or an ORDER BY/tiebreaker design decision, plus verifying no existing duplicate-org_id rows — a schema/data decision, not a mechanical one-line fix.

findings.summary: The new isRetryOfSameCheckout guard only distinguishes 'genuine upgrade' from 'same checkout already applied'; it does not distinguish 'already applied AND already notified' from 'applied but notification never completed'. If the handler throws between the DB writes (which commit and make subBefore look identical on the next attempt) and the TENANT_CREATED emit (e.g. tenantRepo.getOne() throws, or emitTyped throws), Stripe's retry will see subBefore already matching sub_id+plan+status='active' and return early at line 749 before ws.sendToTenant/TENANT_CREATED run at all -- the notification is then never delivered on any future retry.
findings.rootCause: The guard treats DB-write idempotency as a proxy for side-effect completion, but the write commits before the side effects run and there is no separate marker for 'side effects already fired' vs 'DB state already matches'. This exact failure mode existed before this round too (previously via org.billing_status=='active'), so it is not a new regression from this fix, but the fix's own comments claim to solve 'these two side effects were not idempotent' without actually closing this partial-failure gap.
findings.justification: Closing the 'DB write committed but side effect never fired' gap needs a dedicated side-effect-completion marker/outbox-pattern design for the Stripe webhook handler — a non-trivial idempotency redesign, not a mechanical fix.

findings.summary: SharesService.create()/update() perform SELECT SUM(percentual) then INSERT/UPDATE as two separate statements with no transaction, row lock (SELECT...FOR UPDATE), or DB-level cross-row CHECK/trigger enforcing sum<=100. Two concurrent POST /shares for the same work_id, each individually within budget, can both read the same pre-write sum and both commit, persisting >100% total split for a work with no rejection.

softDelete() has no deleted_at IS NULL guard on the UPDATE, no CAS/optimistic lock, no transaction, and DELETE /contracts/:id has no IdempotencyInterceptor (unlike POST /contracts). Concurrent duplicate cancel calls (double-click, retry racing original) can both pass findById() before either commits, both emit CONTRACT_CANCELLED, producing duplicate activity-log rows and duplicate user notifications for one logical cancellation.

Contract softDelete/cancel never calls the e-signature provider (Autentique/DocuSign) to void/cancel the external envelope -- cancelling a contract in MUSIC OS 360 leaves the external signature request active/pending indefinitely. Deferred: no cancel/void call exists in either integration service today; needs a dedicated integration-scoped design (which provider, which envelope id mapping) rather than a quick patch.
findings.justification: Finding explicitly says this 'needs a dedicated integration-scoped design (which provider, which envelope id mapping) rather than a quick patch' — deferred by its own text.

findings.summary: LicensingService.update() validates status only via @IsIn(STATUSES) enum membership with no fromStatus->toStatus legality check (unlike contracts, which uses WorkflowService.getAllowedTransitions/transitionInTx). Any PATCH /licenses/:id can flip status directly e.g. expirada->ativa or ativa->proposta with no illegal-transition protection.

Which transitions are actually legal for a license (e.g. can proposta skip straight to expirada? can ativa revert to negociacao?) is a business-rule decision this session has no authority to invent unilaterally -- doing so risks encoding a wrong rule that blocks a legitimate real-world flow. Recorded for product/domain-owner decision before implementation, not dropped.

findings.summary: Wave 6 cross-review noted the affected=0 test's assertion on repo.update's criteria didn't explicitly check deleted_at: IsNull() was present, only id/tenant_id -- a regression dropping the guard while keeping the mock's affected=0 would still pass. Fixed same pass: assertion now includes deleted_at: IsNull().

ISRC has no DB uniqueness constraint on works or phonograms (only idx_works_isrc / idx_phonograms_isrc, plain non-unique B-tree indexes, unchanged through canonical-order rebuild migrations 20260719000002/3). ISRC is a real-world globally-unique identifier; no product doc/comment found deciding tenant-scoped vs global uniqueness -- the gap looks like an oversight, not a decision. Two rows (same or different tenant) can carry the identical ISRC with zero DB-level protection.
findings.justification: Adding a UNIQUE constraint on ISRC requires a product decision on tenant-scoped vs. global uniqueness plus a backfill/migration to handle any existing duplicates — schema decision, not mechanical.

findings.summary: CreatePhonogramDto.isrc has only @IsString/@MaxLength(20) -- no format validation, no normalization. phonograms.service.ts create()/update() (lines 147-181) writes dto.isrc straight to the entity via repo.create/save with zero transformation. normalizeIsrc/isValidIsrc (apps/api/src/modules/registry/validators/registry-validators.ts:51-56) exist and ARE wired into RecordingRegistryValidationService (registry/validation/entity-validators.ts:144) but that validator only runs inside the collecting-society registry-submission flow (registry/validation/society-validation.service.ts), not on the manual create/update path used by the phonogram/work form. Same gap on works (no isrc validator call found in works.service.ts at all).
findings.justification: Verified: phonograms.service.ts create()/update() now call normalizeIsrc/isValidIsrc on the manual entry path (lines ~151-160), and works.service.ts has an equivalent normalizeIsrcField helper — the validator is no longer confined to the registry-submission flow only.

findings.summary: Bulk CSV import writes isrc via dynamic parameterized INSERT (values parameterized, column names quote()-validated -- no SQL injection) but only applies generic normalizeImportedValue (trim + JSON.parse for {}/[] strings). No ISRC-specific case/hyphen normalization or format validation. Combined with the manual-entry path also skipping normalizeIsrc/isValidIsrc, the same real-world ISRC can be persisted in different textual forms via different write paths (e.g. 'BR-ABC-26-00001' via import vs 'brabc2600001' via manual form), which would defeat even a future UNIQUE(isrc) constraint.
findings.justification: Verified: import-commit.service.ts now applies normalizeIsrc/isValidIsrc specifically to the isrc physical column during bulk import (comment cites find-fb2cfb1b), closing the manual-vs-import normalization mismatch.

findings.summary: phonograms.work_id / phonograms.artist_id (and works.artist_id) have no DB-level FOREIGN KEY at all (CREATE TABLE has no REFERENCES clause; TypeORM @ManyToOne is metadata-only since schema is migration-managed). phonograms.service.ts create() (lines 147-168) persists any client-supplied work_id without checking it belongs to the same tenant_id. Result: (a) orphan risk -- work_id can reference a deleted/nonexistent work with no cascade/restrict, and (b) cross-tenant reference risk -- nothing in DB or service prevents a phonogram in tenant A from pointing work_id at a work owned by tenant B.
findings.justification: Verified: phonograms.service.ts create()/update() now call assertSameTenantFk for work_id and artist_id (comment cites find-f81eebf2), closing both the orphan-reference and cross-tenant-reference gaps.

findings.summary: No DB-level uniqueness constraint on ISRC (works.isrc/phonograms.isrc), neither per-tenant nor global -- only plain lookup indexes idx_works_isrc/idx_phonograms_isrc. Real-world ISRC is a globally-unique industry identifier; nothing here enforces even per-tenant uniqueness, allowing accidental duplicate data entry within one tenant's own catalog.

ISRC has no format validation/normalization on the manual create/update write path (phonograms + works) -- normalizeIsrc/isValidIsrc exist in registry-validators.ts but only run inside the collecting-society registry-submission flow, not at phonogram/work create/update time. Same real ISRC can be persisted in different textual forms across write paths (manual vs bulk import vs external integration), which would defeat even a future uniqueness constraint.

phonograms.work_id/phonograms.artist_id/works.artist_id have no DB-level FOREIGN KEY (InitialSchema CREATE TABLE has no REFERENCES clause) and no application-layer cross-tenant ownership check (unlike shares.service.ts/licensing.service.ts which use assertSameTenantFk). A phonogram in tenant A can silently reference a work_id/artist_id owned by tenant B, or a deleted/nonexistent id, with nothing at DB or service layer preventing it.

Bulk CSV importer writes ISRC via generic normalizeImportedValue (trim + JSON-parse) with no ISRC-specific normalization (uppercase, strip separators) or format validation, unlike the registry-submission validator which has correct logic (registry-validators.ts normalizeIsrc/isValidIsrc) that this path never calls.
Bulk-import ISRC normalization/validation (find-fb2cfb1b) does not cover per-track ISRC inside the releases 'faixas' repeating group; only the flat generalKeys/importableColumns path is checked
findings.rootCause: ImportCommitService.assertValidIsrc() and insertGroup()'s normalizeIsrc-on-insert only iterate def.importableColumns / contract.fields (the RELEASES_CONTRACT general columns, which expose isrc_global but not per-track isrc). RELEASES_CONTRACT.repeatingGroup.fields includes an 'isrc' key per track, but deriveRepeatingItems()/writeReleasesFaixasForImport() write f.isrc straight into releases.metadata.faixas[].isrc with zero normalization or format validation, so a malformed/lowercase/dashed ISRC imported via a release's track list bypasses both the new pre-check and the manual-entry-path normalization that phonograms/works now enforce, leaving inconsistent ISRC text forms depending on entry path for exactly the scenario the fix was meant to close.

findings.justification: Marketing Campaign Builder's competing status vocabulary sharing one physical column with CampaignsService's CampaignStatus, plus no workflow/state-machine registration, is an architectural gap needing a design decision (separate column vs. registered workflow), not a mechanical fix.

findings.summary: campaigns.service.ts update() clobbers previously-stored metadata JSON keys not resent in the current PATCH (e.g. updating only currency wipes out platforms)
findings.rootCause: dtoToEntity() builds out['metadata'] by merging only dto.metadata (if present in THIS request) with this request's currency/platforms; update() never reads current.metadata (already fetched via findById) before building the replacement object. Since TypeORM update() overwrites the whole JSON column rather than merging, any PATCH that sets currency or platforms without resending the full metadata object silently deletes any other previously-stored metadata keys. No test in campaigns.service.spec.ts exercises update() or this merge path at all.

findings.summary: LEAD_CONVERTED idempotency guard is TOCTOU-racy: two near-simultaneous duplicate deliveries for the same lead can both read client_id=null before either write commits, creating duplicate client+artist records

Test coverage (lead-events.handler.spec.ts) only exercises sequential/mocked scenarios, not concurrent delivery.

findings.summary: Systemic missing outbound timeout across most provider integrations: TikTokService, AppleMusicService, SoundCloudService, GoogleAdsService, AbramusService and InstagramService all extend IntegrationBaseService (exposes this.fetch() -> resilientFetch with AbortController timeout + circuit breaker, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=10s) yet call raw global fetch() directly, bypassing it entirely: tiktok.service.ts:46,68,96; apple-music/apple-music.service.ts:68,89; soundcloud/soundcloud.service.ts:40,56,74; google-ads/google-ads.service.ts:64,90; abramus/abramus.service.ts:37,51; instagram/instagram.service.ts:41,45,66,91,123,133,138. YouTubeService and DeezerService (youtube.service.ts:22,43,64; deezer.service.ts:18,36,53,69) don't extend the base class and also use bare fetch() with zero timeout, as does ACRCloudService (acrcloud.service.ts:43). A hanging/slow provider on any of these 9 integrations blocks the calling request indefinitely -- inconsistent with the project's own established resilientFetch/timedFetch pattern correctly used by SoundchartsService, AutentiqueService, DocuSignService and SpotifyService (via CircuitBreakerRegistry.fetch).

Two competing secret-reading mechanisms for the same category of provider secret coexist in integrations/: AutentiqueService, DocuSignService and InstagramService read META_APP_SECRET/webhook secrets via ConfigService.get() (the project's validated config path, backed by apps/api/src/core/config/env.schema.ts), while whatsapp-webhook.controller.ts:112 (META_APP_SECRET) and whatsapp-cloud.provider.ts:107 (WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN) and soundcharts.service.ts:71,81-82 (SOUNDCHARTS_CLIENT_ID/SECRET) read directly from process.env, bypassing ConfigService despite both env vars being declared/validated in env.schema.ts. Functionally equivalent today, but it is an undocumented second config-access pattern for secrets that can silently diverge from ConfigService (e.g. test/module overrides, future schema transforms/defaults) with no single source of truth for how integration secrets are read.
findings.justification: Switched all three files from raw process.env reads to injected ConfigService.get(): whatsapp-webhook.controller.ts (META_APP_SECRET, ConfigService injected into constructor), whatsapp-cloud.provider.ts (WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN, ConfigService injected alongside existing DataSource/EncryptionService deps), soundcharts.service.ts (SOUNDCHARTS_CLIENT_ID/SOUNDCHARTS_CLIENT_SECRET, ConfigService injected as new constructor param; doc comment updated to no longer claim direct process.env reads). Updated the 5 spec files that construct these classes directly (new X(...)) to pass a ConfigService stub reading from process.env. Ran whatsapp-webhook.controller.spec.ts + whatsapp-cloud.provider.spec.ts (25 passed) and soundcharts.service.spec.ts + soundcharts-canonical-candidates.util.spec.ts + soundcharts-metric-mapping.spec.ts (54 passed).

findings.summary: instagram.service.spec.ts revocation test does not actually prove the guarded-fetch fix
findings.rootCause: The updated assertion uses expect.objectContaining({ method: 'DELETE' }) instead of the prior exact-match assert. Since the test mocks global.fetch directly (not this.fetch), and this.fetch/resilientFetch ultimately still calls global fetch with the same init plus an added signal field, objectContaining({method:'DELETE'}) matches both the fixed code (call includes signal) AND the pre-fix raw fetch call (no signal). Reverting the fix (removing this.fetch -> fetch) would leave this test green, so it is a false-green / weak-assertion regression test per testing.md's false-green-prevention rule. A meaningful fix would assert init.signal is an AbortSignal, matching the pattern already used correctly in the new youtube.service.spec.ts test.
findings.justification: Verified fix: expect(deleteInit.signal).toBeInstanceOf(AbortSignal) added to the /me/permissions DELETE assertion in instagram.service.spec.ts. disconnectProvider makes exactly one fetch call (the DELETE) when conn.accessToken exists, so fetchMock.mock.calls.find(...)! is safe (never returns undefined here). resilientFetch always spreads init and adds signal:controller.signal before invoking global fetch, so reverting this.fetch()->fetch() would leave deleteInit.signal undefined and the toBeInstanceOf(AbortSignal) assertion would throw an AssertionError (test fails on revert, as intended). AbortSignal confirmed as a real Node global in this repo's jest testEnvironment:node (Node v24) -- no ReferenceError risk. Adversarial review found no issue.

findings.summary: Idempotency cache key is '{userId}:{idempotencyKey}' with NO tenant/org component (JwtAuth.orgId ignored). A user who is a member of 2+ tenants (multi-org membership is the auth model here: JwtAuth carries a per-token orgId while userId is the stable auth-provider id) and replays the same client-generated X-Idempotency-Key while acting in a different tenant context gets the OTHER tenant's cached response body/statusCode replayed verbatim (executeAndCache stores by userId+key only, IdempotencyStore has no tenant awareness). This is a cross-tenant response-data leak via cache, not just a duplicate-execution bug. Fix pattern: include tenant/org id in the cache key, e.g. '{orgId}:{userId}:{idempotencyKey}'.

NotificationsProcessor.handleSend has no idempotency guard: every job invocation does repo.create()+repo.save() unconditionally, and no jobId/dedup key is passed at enqueue (notifications-queue.service.ts queue.add calls omit {jobId}). Under BullMQ's at-least-once delivery (stalled-job recovery re-picking up a job whose DB write already committed but whose ack was lost, or an operator manually retrying a 'failed' job after partial success), a duplicate notification row is persisted and a duplicate WS push (notification:new) is sent to the user. No unique constraint on (tenant_id, user_id, entity, entity_id, type) or similar to make the insert idempotent at the DB level either.

findings.summary: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX (non-CONCURRENTLY) on works/phonograms takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and does a full-table scan while building; on a large works/phonograms table this blocks all reads and writes for the duration. The migration's own comment documents that it was NOT executed against any real DB this session and requires the standard db:migrate authorization flow — flagging for the eventual production run: use CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (run outside the migration's implicit transaction, TypeORM migrations run each migration in a transaction by default) or schedule during a maintenance window, and run the documented pre-check query first since a duplicate-data failure happens only after the scan completes.
findings.justification: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block, and TypeORM's migration runner wraps each migration in a transaction by default -- switching to CONCURRENTLY requires either a migration-runner-level opt-out mechanism (transaction: false / per-migration config) this codebase doesn't currently expose, or restructuring the migration to run outside the standard runner. The migration is confirmed NOT YET EXECUTED against any real database (per its own migration-safety documentation, consistent with this session's pattern of writing+registering but never running migrations). Recorded for the actual production/staging rollout decision (which needs the migration-runner opt-out mechanism designed first), not dropped.

findings.summary: AIJobsProcessor.process() calls dbContext.runInTenantContext({tenantId: d.tenantId, ...}) without first checking d.tenantId is present, unlike every sibling processor (ExternalDataProcessor, ArtistPlatformSyncProcessor, MarketBenchmarkRefreshProcessor, MarketingPublishingProcessor, NotificationsProcessor) which all fail-closed with an explicit guard ('job sem tenantId — abortado'/throw) before touching tenant-scoped data. RLS still fail-closed-denies here (empty session var never matches a real tenant_id) so this is not a cross-tenant read risk, but a malformed/missing-tenantId AI job surfaces as an unhandled DB/uuid-cast error deep in the transaction instead of a clean guard message, and (depending on AIService.complete's error handling) could still attempt provider calls or partial side effects before the DB write fails.

MarketingPublishingProcessor.processContent is a check-then-act race with no row lock/transaction: reads row, checks row.status==='agendado' && publication_status!=='published', THEN issues a separate UPDATE to set publication_status='publishing'. If the same content is enqueued twice (duplicate scheduler tick, manual retry while a job is still in-flight, or two BullMQ workers under a misconfigured concurrency>1 with the same jobId not enforced), both can pass the read-check before either writes 'publishing', and both proceed to call this.publish(row) concurrently -> duplicate publish attempt against the external platform API. Same TOCTOU pattern already fixed elsewhere in this codebase (dunning lock) via pg_advisory_xact_lock; not applied here. Lower likelihood than P1 (BullMQ job-level locking + the fail-closed tenant guard reduce but do not eliminate the window: two independently-enqueued jobs for the same contentId are not deduplicated at the queue level).
Notification BullMQ redelivery dedup is a check-then-insert race, not atomic
findings.rootCause: handleSend() does a SELECT (metadata->>'bullmq_job_id') then INSERT inside separate statements with no unique constraint/index and no SELECT...FOR UPDATE. If BullMQ marks a job stalled (lock TTL expiry while a worker is still finishing) and reassigns it to a second worker while the first is still running -- a documented BullMQ at-least-once scenario -- both workers can pass the 'existing == null' check concurrently and both INSERT, producing two notification rows and two WS pushes for the same job.id. The sibling fix in marketing-publishing.processor.ts (same wave, find-61333a55) closes the analogous race correctly with an atomic UPDATE...WHERE + affected-count check; the notifications processor was not given the same treatment despite documenting the identical threat model in its own comment (find-8dfe93c3).

23505 catch-and-refetch in handleSend re-throws instead of recovering the winner's row when DATABASE_SESSION_CONTEXT_ENABLED=true (staging/production config)
findings.rootCause: runInTenantContext wraps handleSend's work in a single Postgres transaction (queryRunner.startTransaction()) when the session-context flag is on. When repo.save(entity) hits the new partial-unique-index violation (23505), the catch block calls findByJobId() again on the SAME queryRunner/transaction to fetch the winner's row -- but Postgres has already aborted that transaction after the failed statement, so any further query on it fails with error 25P02 ('current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block'). That new error is not a 23505 and is not caught, so it propagates out of runInTenantContext (which rolls back and rethrows), causing handleSend to throw instead of returning alreadyExisted=true with the winner's row -- exactly the outcome the fix was meant to prevent. This only manifests when DATABASE_SESSION_CONTEXT_ENABLED=true, which is the actual staging config (.env.staging, .github/workflows/staging.yml) and the documented target for production (docs/runbooks/release-baseline-157-80.md), i.e. precisely the environment where concurrent-worker races are real (separate connections/transactions). The new regression test in notifications.processor.spec.ts uses a hard-coded passthrough mock (mockDbContext.runInTenantContext = (ctx, work) => work(undefined)) that always exercises the flag-OFF, non-transactional code path, so it can never catch this. Fix: use a SAVEPOINT before the INSERT attempt (and ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT before the re-fetch), or move the re-fetch to a fresh connection/queryRunner outside the aborted transaction.

findings.summary: listArtists() builds qb.orderBy(`a.${orderField}`, ...) from query.orderBy (PaginationDto, unrestricted client string, only @IsOptional/@IsString validated) with ZERO allow-list check -- unlike the 3 sibling services (marketing-projects/contents/assets) which each validate orderBy against an allow-list (though duplicated ad hoc instead of using the shared safe-order-by.ts util, which existed but was never wired anywhere). TypeORM's QueryBuilder.orderBy() concatenates the column expression directly into SQL (columns cannot be parameterized), so an attacker-controlled orderBy value is a live SQL injection vector on the artists list endpoint (e.g. ORDER BY subquery-based blind/time-based injection). Discovered while auditing safe-order-by.ts's disposition (req-a0341efe/ac-bfe83ea7) -- it was unused precisely because this call site never adopted it.
findings.justification: Fixed: artists.service.ts now uses safeOrderBy() with an allow-list (nome_artistico/status/status_cadastro/created_at/updated_at) and 'created_at' fallback, closing the ORDER BY SQL injection. Also wired safeOrderBy into the 3 sibling services (marketing-projects/contents/assets) that had ad hoc equivalent validation, consolidating on one implementation. Verified: tsc 0 errors, artists+marketing test suites green (335+24 tests), independent security-reviewer PASS (evid-2658b629) confirming no residual injection surface and no other unguarded ORDER BY call site in the codebase.

findings.summary: The 'transitions to read_only via a WHERE-guarded UPDATE' test called service.getStateWithEscalation('tenant-1') with no way to inject a fixed clock -- applyOverrideAndEscalation's internal now=new Date() default always used the REAL wall clock, while the test's own 'now' variable (2026-09-03) was unused/decorative. As real time progressed past the suspend_after_days threshold relative to the hardcoded grace_until (2026-09-01), the test started failing for real (escalating to 'suspended' instead of the expected 'read_only') -- discovered live during a full-suite regression run in this session (crossed the threshold around 2026-09-12/13 UTC). A ticking time bomb, unrelated to any change in this mission. Fixed with jest.useFakeTimers({ now }) scoped to that one test (test-only fix, zero production code touched).
findings.justification: jest.useFakeTimers({ now }) added around the affected test, restored in a finally block. Verified: billing-enforcement.service.spec.ts 22/22 pass with the log line confirming the pinned clock (02/09/2026 21:00:00 vs real time). Also checked other tests in the same describe block ('when a concurrent writer...') already correctly pass an explicit now to applyOverrideAndEscalation and are unaffected.
